docs.text: NOAA's Great Lakes Environmental Research Lab is being forced to suspend communications due to staff cuts. GLERL provided critical weekly updates about extent and impact of harmful algal blooms in Lake Erie — including the 2014 bloom that left Toledo and parts of NW Ohio without drinking water.

Took the day off yesterday to do some volunteer urban stream sampling with the Huron River Watershed Council's chemistry & flow monitoring program! I got to sample with Kelly, the program director + my friend, to sample the "downriver" sites that flow into Lake Erie

Check out our new success story featuring Cleveland Water Alliance. Along with dozens of regional partner organizations, CWA has deployed more than 200 sensors to water sources throughout the Lake Erie region in an effort to prevent water quality disasters. www.healthylakes.org/latest-updat...

A Great Lakes Early Warning System framework would allow researchers and governments to detect and address water quality threats before they become established. *June 13 webinar: www.ijc.org/en/sab/GLEWS...

Areas of Concern are the most toxic & contaminated sites in the Great Lakes region, but Great Lakes Restoration Initiative funding has accelerated the clean-up of these sites 💧 #GreatLakes #CleanWater #HealthyLakes
A potential cyber breach at a Great Lakes Water Authority treatment facility in Detroit is under investigation.

(2/5) NOAA was told to dismantle the program that monitors the health of The Great Lakes. This staff monitored toxic algae blooms, ice coverage, clean drinking water, and invasive species such as Asian carp and lamprey eels. The Great Lakes contain more than 20% of the world's fresh surface water.

In Michigan’s Western Lake Erie Basin, our coalition implemented a network of water monitors at 50 locations. The sensors' data is giving state leaders, farmers, and conservation groups better tools to reduce phosphorus pollution and harmful algal blooms.
